title: First Aid Basics
summary: Simple first aid steps for cuts, burns, nosebleeds, and heat illness, and when to call for help.
poll: Every student should learn first aid at school.

versions.title: Help Fast
versions.text:
You trip and cut your knee. What do you do? You use first aid. It is the help you give right away.

First, stay calm. Look to see if the place is safe. Then get an adult. If it is bad, call 997. That will bring help fast.

Now, a small cut. Wash your hands. Rinse the cut with clean water. If it bleeds, press on it with a clean cloth. Hold it. Then put on a bandage.

Next, a small burn. Hold it under cool tap water. Keep it there for a long time, up to twenty minutes. Do not use ice. Do not put on butter.

Next, a nose bleed. Sit down. Lean a bit forward. Do not tip your head back. Pinch the soft part of your nose for ten minutes.

On hot days, you may feel sick and dizzy. Go to the shade. Drink some water. Rest.

A home needs a first aid kit. It holds bandages and gloves. Know where it is!

versions.title: Help Fast
versions.text:
You trip and cut your knee. What should you do? You can use first aid. First aid is the help you give right away, before a doctor comes.

First, stay calm. Check that the place is safe. Then tell an adult. If someone is badly hurt, call 997. In Saudi Arabia, that number brings an ambulance.

For a small cut, wash your hands first. Rinse the cut with clean water. If it bleeds, press on it with a clean cloth. Hold it until it stops. Then cover it with a bandage.

For a small burn, hold it under cool running water. Keep it there for about twenty minutes. Do not use ice or butter.

For a nose bleed, sit down and lean a bit forward. Do not tip your head back. Pinch the soft part of your nose for ten minutes.

On very hot days, you may feel dizzy and sick. Move to the shade. Sip cool water and rest.

Every home should have a first aid kit. It holds bandages, gloves, and more. Find out where yours is!

versions.title: First Aid Basics
versions.text:
Imagine you trip on the playground and scrape your knee. What should you do next? This is where first aid helps. First aid is the care given right away after an injury, before a doctor or nurse arrives. Knowing a few simple steps can help you stay calm and be useful.

The first step is always to make sure the place is safe. You should not rush into danger, such as a busy road. Next, tell an adult what happened. If someone is badly hurt, call 997 for an ambulance from the Saudi Red Crescent.

For a small cut, wash your hands first. Then rinse the cut gently with clean water to remove dirt. If it is bleeding, use a clean cloth to put firm pressure on it until the bleeding stops. Finally, cover it with a bandage to keep germs out.

For a minor burn, cool the skin under cool running water for about twenty minutes. Never use ice, butter, or toothpaste, because they can damage the skin.

For a nosebleed, sit down and lean slightly forward, so the blood does not run down the throat. Pinch the soft part of the nose for about ten minutes.

In hot weather, a person who has not had enough water may feel dizzy, weak, and sick. Help them move into the shade, give them sips of cool water, and let them rest. If they get confused or faint, call for help at once.

Every home and school should have a first aid kit with bandages, gloves, and other supplies. Find out where yours is kept.

Imagine you trip on the playground and scrape your knee. What should you do next? This is where first aid comes in. First aid is the care given immediately after an injury, before professional medical help arrives. Learning a few simple steps can help you remain calm and be genuinely useful in a difficult moment.

The first step is always to make sure the area is safe. You should never rush into danger, such as a busy road, to reach someone. Next, tell an adult what happened. If someone is seriously hurt, call 997 to request an ambulance from the Saudi Red Crescent.

For a small cut, wash your hands first. Then rinse the cut gently with clean water to remove any dirt. If it is bleeding, use a clean cloth to apply firm pressure until the bleeding stops. Finally, cover the wound with a bandage to keep germs out.

For a minor burn, cool the skin under cool running water for about twenty minutes. Never use ice, butter, or toothpaste, because these can damage the skin further.

For a nosebleed, sit down and lean slightly forward, so the blood does not run down the throat. Pinch the soft part of the nose firmly for about ten minutes without letting go.

In hot weather, a person who has not had enough water may feel dizzy, weak, and nauseous. Help them move into the shade, offer small sips of cool water, and let them rest. If they become confused or faint, call for emergency help immediately.

Every home and school should keep a first aid kit stocked with bandages, gloves, and other supplies. Make sure you know exactly where yours is stored.

versions.title: First Aid Basics
versions.text:
Imagine you trip on the playground and scrape your knee. What should you do next? This is precisely where first aid becomes important. First aid is the care given immediately after an injury or sudden illness, before professional medical help arrives, and mastering a few simple procedures can help you remain calm and be genuinely useful.

Your first priority is always to assess the situation and confirm that the area is safe, because rushing into danger, such as a busy road, could create a second victim. Next, inform an adult about what happened. If someone is seriously injured, call 997 to request an ambulance from the Saudi Red Crescent.

For a small cut, wash your hands first, and then rinse the cut gently with clean water to remove dirt that could cause an infection. If it is bleeding, apply firm pressure with a clean cloth until the bleeding stops. Finally, cover the wound with a clean bandage.

For a minor burn, cool the skin under cool running water for approximately twenty minutes. Never apply ice, butter, or toothpaste, which can damage the skin further. If a blister develops, do not pop it, because the blister protects the delicate skin underneath from germs.

For a nosebleed, sit down and lean slightly forward, so that the blood does not run down the throat. Pinch the soft part of the nose firmly for approximately ten minutes without releasing it.

During the intense Saudi summer, a person who has not consumed enough water may feel dizzy, weak, and nauseous. Move them into the shade, offer small sips of cool water, and let them rest. However, if they become confused or faint, they may be suffering from heatstroke, which is a medical emergency, so call for help immediately.

Every home and school should keep a first aid kit stocked with bandages, disposable gloves, and other supplies, and everyone should know exactly where it is stored.

The first priority is always to assess the situation and confirm that the surroundings are safe, because rushing into danger, such as heavy traffic, could easily create a second victim. Afterwards, inform a responsible adult. If someone is seriously injured, call 997 to request an ambulance from the Saudi Red Crescent, and describe the location and the problem clearly.

To treat a minor cut, wash your hands, and then rinse the wound gently with clean water to remove dirt that could otherwise cause an infection. If it continues bleeding, apply firm, steady pressure with a clean cloth until the bleeding stops, and finally cover the wound with a clean bandage.

For a minor burn, cool the affected skin under cool running water for approximately twenty minutes, which draws heat out of the damaged tissue. Never apply ice, butter, or toothpaste, since these can damage the skin further. If a blister develops, do not pop it, because the blister protects the delicate skin underneath from germs.

For a nosebleed, sit down and lean slightly forward, so that blood does not run down the throat, and pinch the soft part of the nose firmly for approximately ten minutes.

During the intense Saudi summer, someone who has not consumed enough water may feel dizzy, weak, and nauseous. Move the person into the shade, offer small sips of cool water, and encourage rest. However, confusion or fainting can indicate heatstroke, a dangerous medical emergency, so call for professional help immediately.

Finally, every household and school should maintain a first aid kit containing bandages, disposable gloves, and other essential supplies, and everyone should know exactly where it is stored.

versions.title: First Aid Basics: Helping in the First Few Minutes
versions.text:
Imagine, for a moment, that a classmate stumbles on the playground and sustains a severe scrape to the knee. What course of action should follow immediately? This is precisely the moment at which the principles of first aid become indispensable. First aid is the immediate care given in the aftermath of an injury or sudden illness, before the arrival of professional medical help, and a working knowledge of a handful of straightforward steps enables ordinary people to remain calm and genuinely useful amid alarming and unpredictable situations.

The foremost priority is always to assess the surrounding situation and confirm that the immediate environment is reasonably safe, since rushing impulsively into evident danger, such as oncoming traffic, risks creating a second casualty in addition to the first. Only once safety has been established should one immediately tell a responsible adult. Should someone be seriously injured, one should telephone 997 to summon an ambulance from the Saudi Red Crescent, describing both the location and the nature of the emergency as clearly as circumstances permit, since precise information allows paramedics to arrive more quickly.

In treating a minor cut, one should first wash the hands thoroughly, then gently rinse the wound itself with clean water in order to remove any dirt that might otherwise lead to infection, and should bleeding continue, firm and steady pressure applied with a clean cloth until the bleeding stops is appropriate, followed finally by covering the wound with a sterile bandage.

For a minor burn, the affected skin should be cooled under gently running water for about twenty minutes, a process that gradually draws heat out of the damaged tissue and considerably reduces pain. Ice, butter, and toothpaste should never be applied, since each of these substances can cause further damage to already injured skin. Should a blister develop, one should resist the urge to pop it deliberately, because the intact blister protects the delicate skin underneath from harmful germs.

In the case of a nosebleed, the affected person should sit upright and lean slightly forward, so that blood does not run down the throat, while firmly pinching the soft part of the nose for about ten uninterrupted minutes.

During the especially intense Saudi summer, someone who has not drunk enough water may begin to feel dizzy, weak, and nauseated. Such a person should be moved promptly into shade, offered small sips of cool water, and encouraged to rest quietly. Confusion or fainting, however, can signal heatstroke, a genuinely dangerous medical emergency in which the body loses the ability to regulate its own temperature effectively, so professional help should be called without delay.

Finally, every household and school ought to keep a well-stocked first aid kit containing bandages, disposable gloves, antiseptic wipes, and other essential supplies, and everyone should know precisely where that kit is stored, since frantic searching during a real emergency wastes valuable, irreplaceable minutes.

versions.title: First Aid Basics: Helping in the First Few Minutes
versions.text:
Imagine, for a moment, that a classmate stumbles unexpectedly on the playground and sustains a severe abrasion to the knee. What course of action ought logically to follow in the immediate aftermath? This is precisely the critical juncture at which the fundamental principles of first aid become genuinely indispensable. First aid denotes the immediate, improvised care administered in the aftermath of an injury or sudden illness, prior to the arrival of qualified professional medical assistance, and a working familiarity with merely a handful of straightforward procedures enables ordinary, untrained individuals to remain composed and demonstrably useful amid alarming and inherently unpredictable circumstances.

The foremost priority, in virtually every scenario, is to assess the surrounding situation comprehensively and confirm that the immediate environment is reasonably safe before proceeding further, since rushing impulsively into evident danger, such as oncoming vehicular traffic, risks inadvertently creating a second casualty in addition to the first. Only once safety has been reasonably established should one immediately inform a responsible adult of the situation. Should an individual be seriously injured, one should telephone 997 without hesitation to summon an ambulance from the Saudi Red Crescent, describing both the precise geographic location and the exact nature of the emergency as clearly and accurately as circumstances permit, since precise, unambiguous information allows responding paramedics to arrive at the scene considerably more rapidly.

In treating a comparatively minor laceration, one should first wash the hands thoroughly with soap, then gently irrigate the wound itself with clean water in order to dislodge any embedded debris that might otherwise precipitate a subsequent infection. Should bleeding persist beyond an initial moment, firm and continuous manual pressure applied with a clean cloth until the bleeding demonstrably ceases is the appropriate response, followed finally by covering the cleaned wound with a sterile adhesive bandage.

For a minor thermal burn, the affected skin should be cooled beneath gently running water for approximately twenty continuous minutes, a process that gradually draws residual heat out of the damaged underlying tissue and substantially reduces accompanying pain. Ice, butter, and toothpaste should categorically never be applied to burned skin, since each of these common household substances can inflict further, avoidable damage upon tissue already compromised. Should a blister subsequently develop at the site, one should resist any temptation to puncture it deliberately, because the intact blister serves a genuinely protective function, shielding the delicate underlying skin from potentially harmful microbial contamination.

In the case of a nosebleed, the affected individual should sit upright and lean slightly forward, thereby preventing blood from draining uncomfortably down the throat, while firmly pinching the soft cartilaginous portion of the nose for approximately ten wholly uninterrupted minutes.

During the especially intense Saudi summer months, an individual who has failed to consume sufficient water may begin to feel dizzy, weak, and nauseated in relatively short order. Such a person should be moved promptly into available shade, offered small, carefully measured sips of cool water, and encouraged to rest quietly until symptoms subside. Confusion or outright fainting, however, can signal heatstroke, a genuinely life-threatening medical emergency in which the body has lost the physiological capacity to regulate its own internal temperature effectively, and professional medical assistance should therefore be summoned without any delay whatsoever.

Finally, every household and educational institution ought, as a matter of basic preparedness, to maintain a well-stocked first aid kit containing bandages, disposable gloves, antiseptic wipes, and other essential supplies, and every occupant should know with absolute certainty precisely where that kit is permanently stored, since frantic, disorganized searching during a genuine emergency squanders valuable, and potentially irreplaceable, minutes.

keyWords.definition: a strip of cloth or a small pad that covers a cut
keyWords.example: The nurse put a bandage on my brother's finger.

keyWords.definition: to lose blood from a cut or wound
keyWords.example: My lip started to bleed when I fell off my bike.

keyWords.definition: a hurt on the skin caused by something very hot
keyWords.example: She got a small burn from the hot pan.

keyWords.definition: quiet and not upset or scared
keyWords.example: The teacher stayed calm when the fire bell rang.

keyWords.definition: a box or bag that holds the tools for a job
keyWords.example: Dad keeps a tool kit in the car.

questions.stem: What is this article mostly about?
options: How doctors and nurses work in big hospitals
Simple ways to help someone who gets hurt
How to play safely on a slide
Why people get sick in winter
questions.why: The article tells what first aid is and gives simple steps for cuts, burns, nose bleeds, and hot days.

wrong.A: Doctors are named, but the article is about help you give before a doctor comes.
wrong.C: A fall is only used to start the article.
wrong.D: The article is about hot days, not winter.

questions.stem: What number can you call in Saudi Arabia when someone is badly hurt?
questions.why: The article says to call 997 to bring help fast.

wrong.A: 555 is not the number in the article.
wrong.B: 100 is not the number in the article.
wrong.D: 123 is not the number in the article.

questions.stem: What should you do first for a small burn?
options: Hold it under cool running water
Put a bag of ice right on it
Rub some butter all over it
Cover it with a warm towel
questions.why: The article says to hold a burn under cool water for up to twenty minutes.

wrong.B: The article says do not use ice.
wrong.C: The article says do not put on butter.
wrong.D: Heat would not help a burn, and the article does not say this.

questions.stem: Why should you lean forward, not back, when your nose bleeds?
options: So you can see the floor
So the blood does not run down your throat
So your nose gets cold
So you fall asleep
questions.why: Leaning forward lets the blood come out instead of going down your throat.

wrong.A: Seeing the floor is not the reason.
wrong.C: Leaning does not make the nose cold.
wrong.D: You should not sleep; you should pinch your nose.

questions.stem: Read this: "Stay calm." What does calm mean?
options: Fast, loud, and angry
Hungry and tired
Very cold and wet
Quiet and not upset
questions.why: Being calm means you are not upset, so you can think and help.

wrong.A: Fast and loud is the opposite of calm.
wrong.C: Calm here is about feelings, not temperature.

questions.stem: What should you do right after you wash your hands to care for a small cut?
options: Rinse the cut with clean water
Put on the bandage
Call an ambulance
Put butter on it
questions.why: The article says wash your hands, then rinse the cut, then press if it bleeds, then put on a bandage.

wrong.C: An ambulance is for someone badly hurt, not a small cut.
wrong.D: Butter is never used in first aid.

questions.stem: A friend feels dizzy after playing in the sun. What is the best thing to do?
options: Keep playing in the sun to feel better
Take a long, hot bath at home
Run around the field to cool off
Help them into the shade and give water
questions.why: The article says to go to the shade, drink water, and rest on hot days.

wrong.A: More play in the sun can make it worse.
wrong.B: Heat will not help someone who is too hot.
wrong.C: Running in the sun can make it worse.

questions.stem: Why does the author start with a story about cutting your knee?
options: To show how to make a bandage
To help readers picture when first aid is needed
To tell about a sports game
To explain how knees work
questions.why: The short scene helps readers imagine a real time they might need first aid.

wrong.A: The article does not show how to make a bandage.
wrong.D: The article does not explain how knees work.

LOW.prompt: Choose one injury from the article. Write the first aid steps in order.
checklist: I wrote the steps in the right order.
I used a key word such as bandage, bleed, or burn.
LOW.modelAnswer: I chose a small cut. First, I would wash my hands to stay clean. Next, I would rinse the cut with clean water. If it was bleeding, I would press a clean cloth on it until it stopped. Finally, I would cover the cut with a bandage to keep out germs.

keyWords.definition: harm done to the body, such as a cut or a broken bone
keyWords.example: The player missed the match because of a leg injury.

keyWords.definition: the force of pushing on something
keyWords.example: Press with steady pressure to stick the poster to the wall.

keyWords.definition: to wash something quickly with clean water
keyWords.example: Rinse the grapes before you eat them.

keyWords.definition: a vehicle that takes sick or hurt people to the hospital
keyWords.example: The ambulance raced past us with its lights flashing.

keyWords.definition: feeling as if things are spinning and you might fall
keyWords.example: I felt dizzy after spinning around on the playground.

questions.stem: What is the central idea of the article?
options: Only doctors should help people who are hurt.
Knowing a few simple first aid steps helps you help others safely.
Burns are the most common injury.
Every injury needs an ambulance.
questions.why: The article explains simple, safe steps for common injuries and when to call for help.

wrong.A: The article teaches readers how to give first aid before a doctor comes.
wrong.C: The article does not say which injury is most common.
wrong.D: The article says to call an ambulance only when someone is seriously hurt.

questions.stem: Why should you check that the area is safe before helping?

So the ambulance arrives faster
So the cut stops bleeding
So you can find the first aid kit

wrong.C: Checking the area does not stop bleeding.
wrong.D: The kit is a separate point in the article.

Leave it open to the air
Press firmly on it with a clean cloth
Put toothpaste on it

wrong.B: The article says to press on it and then cover it.

questions.stem: Read this: "use a clean cloth to put firm pressure on it." What does pressure mean?

A pushing force
A kind of medicine
A loud sound

wrong.D: Pressure is not a sound.

questions.stem: Why does the article say never to put ice, butter, or toothpaste on a burn?
options: They make the water too cold
They are hard to find
They can damage the skin
They help the burn heal too fast

wrong.B: The article does not talk about finding them.
wrong.D: Nothing in the article says they help healing.

questions.stem: A person in the hot sun becomes confused and faints. What should you do?
options: Give them a snack and wait
Call for emergency help at once
Tell them to walk home
Pinch their nose for ten minutes

wrong.C: A confused person should not walk home alone in the heat.

MID.prompt: Explain what you would do, step by step, if a classmate became dizzy on a very hot day. Tell when you would call 997.
checklist: I described moving to shade, water, and rest.
I explained the warning signs that mean calling for help.
I used at least two key words.
MID.modelAnswer: If a classmate became dizzy on a hot day, I would first help them move into the shade and let them rest. Then I would offer small sips of cool water so they could recover from feeling dizzy. I would call 997 for an ambulance right away if the classmate became confused or fainted, because that means it could be a serious injury that needs professional help.

HIGH.prompt: Explain how a first aider should decide what to do first and when to call for professional help. Use at least two examples from the article.
checklist: I explained why assessing safety comes first.
I gave two examples of first aid steps.
I described signs that mean calling 997.
HIGH.modelAnswer: A good first aider must always assess the situation first, because the top priority is making sure the area is safe before helping anyone. For example, with a bleeding cut, you should rinse it and apply pressure before covering it with a bandage to prevent infection. For a burn, you should cool the skin under running water for about twenty minutes instead of using ice or butter. If someone shows signs like confusion or fainting, possibly from heatstroke, that is when you must call 997 immediately instead of trying to handle it yourself.
